messages:
maria: Heads-up — Dependabot flagged a high-severity CVE in tokenizers wheels (CVE-2026-9999). We attempted a poetry update and now CI is red across py39/py310 manylinux builds.

alex: I pulled the failing job logs — wheel build is failing during auditwheel step with undefined symbol errors when building with our manylinux container. Not a tox/test failure, packaging.

sam: ci-bot shows: 
```
ci-bot: Build step failed: auditwheel repair produced invalid ELF: undefined symbol: PyUnicode_ReadChar
Exit code: 1
```

maria: That undefined symbol smells like a mismatch between the tokenizers binary wheel and our base glibc / python ABI in the manylinux image. Could be the new prebuilt wheel was built against newer CPython or patched Rust flags.

alex: Agree. Quick triage options: 1) revert tokenizers upgrade in poetry.lock (fast); 2) vendor-build tokenizers from source on our CI (slow, flakey); 3) pin to an earlier compatible wheel for CI only (temp); 4) move to a patched manylinux image (infra change). Thoughts? :thinking:

sam: For short term we should revert lock to last known-good and open a follow-up to investigate upstream wheel compatibility. Revert means regen lock and patch the PR for the security fix later.

jordan: Revert plus a staging-only test where we build tokenizers from source and run a smoke test. If build-from-source passes, we can coordinate with infra to decide whether to upgrade manylinux or ask upstream to re-release.

maria: Security tradeoff: the CVE is real; we need to ensure we don't leave users exposed. Reverting the upgrade delays the CVE fix for prod. Can we patch by applying the minimal security fix from the upstream tokenizers release without taking the new wheel? i.e., vendor the patched C code or apply backport?

alex: Backporting tokenizers C/Rust fix into our repo is non-trivial and not safe for quick patch. I'd prefer revert and a canary deploy of the patched wheel on non-prod (dedicated env) to validate.

sam: I'll open a revert PR now that pins tokenizers to 0.14.2 in poetry.lock and adds a CI matrix exclusion for the new wheel. Also adding an item to the PR description: "blocked by tokenizers wheel compatibility investigation" and link to this thread.

ci-bot: PR created: #4123 — revert/tokenizers-0.14.2-lock (maria). CI triggered.

maria: Thanks. After revert merges, we should create a small runbook for future wheel compatibility issues: checklist (auditwheel logs, python abi check, manylinux image hash, rust toolchain used). I'll draft it.

jordan: Also flag infra — possible to test new manylinux image in a parallel CI job so future wheels can be validated before we merge dependency upgrades.

alex: Action items: 
- sam: open revert PR and add CI exclusion (in flight).
- maria: draft wheel-compat runbook and steps to validate upstream wheel.
- jordan: sync with infra about a parallel "wheel-compat" job.
- sam: follow-up issue to reapply CVE fix after we validate new wheel or backport.

maria: tagging sec-assessment: we also need to document the temporary exposure window in the tracker and email the small set of customers on Dedicated that we may not have patched yet. I'll start a short note. :memo:
